extraction.name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
extraction.description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing, comprising 10,497 curated examples across 13 task categories.
extraction.creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was built by extracting diverse visual and auditory inputs from 47 source datasets, curating role-play texts from RoleBench, synthesizing speech instructions with three TTS models, transcribing synthesized audio with Whisper-Large-v3, and performing multi-stage manual curation including deduplication, validation, categorization, and balanced sampling.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Incomplete or unsuitable instances were excluded, including entries with corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, and demonstrably incorrect answers. Approximately 10% of candidates were discarded during validation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source data were drawn from 47 datasets spanning audio, speech, music, dialogue, vision, and multimodal tasks, including MMMU, RoleBench, VoiceBench, VocalBench, AIR-Bench, SD-Eval, AudioCaps, LibriSpeech, Common Voice, Clotho, MusicCaps, VCTK, and others.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Text instructions were rewritten for TTS suitability, special image tokens were replaced with descriptive phrases, multiple-choice options were rephrased for readability, speech was synthesized using F5-TTS, ChatTTS, and Dia-1.6B, low-quality clips were regenerated until UTMOS exceeded 3.8, and the synthesized audio was transcribed with Whisper-Large-v3 and the lowest-WER sample retained.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Deduplication used lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance, followed by manual review; incomplete or unsuitable items were removed; remaining examples were assigned to 13 task categories; and balanced sampling was applied to equalize category representation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human curators reviewed candidate items and assigned Good/Bad verdicts during curation. The benchmark also uses evaluator prompts to produce labels such as Correct/Incorrect or Good/Bad for model outputs, but the paper does not describe a separate human annotation labeling workflow beyond curation and evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports human evaluation validation for the automated scoring scheme, including Pearson correlations and agreement rates between gpt-oss-20b judgments and human ratings. It also notes that the final benchmark uses curated examples after manual review and that the evaluation combines content, speech, and consistency scores.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Whisper-Large-v3, UTMOS, UTMOS Strong, gpt-oss-20b, emotion2vec, Wespeaker, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, F5-TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and code will be publicly released under an MIT license. The authors state they will maintain a data governance process for auditing and removal and reserve the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Voice/timbre and speaker identity-related information are included through role-play voice imitation and speaker similarity evaluation; the paper also mentions user emotions and roles. It emphasizes consent, provenance, and anti-impersonation safeguards.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to improve evaluation of voice assistants for real-world applications such as healthcare, education, smart homes, customer service, and automotive use. The paper also discusses risks of impersonation, privacy violations, harassment, fraud, and unequal performance across demographics.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes potential biases from source data and design choices, including academic or synthetic sources, a fixed set of 100 roles that may encode stereotypes or omit important personas, and unequal performance across demographics.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is limited in diversity, is monolingual with all prompts and evaluations in English except five Chinese roles, evaluates only one proprietary model, uses automated and GPT-based scoring that may introduce noise and bias, lacks video-audio integration and continuous streaming tasks, and is offline/static rather than interactive.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Intended for evaluation, benchmarking, testing, and longitudinal assessment of voice assistants; not intended for training models for cheating. The paper also frames it as useful for research on listening, speaking, viewing, personalization, robustness, safety, and multimodal understanding.
